listingTitle: Keep untrusted workflow data out of shell templates
title: Keep untrusted workflow data out of shell templates
why: GitHub expands expressions before invoking the shell, so attacker-controlled event or dispatch values can inject commands into a generated script.
suggestion: Assign the expression to an env value, validate it where appropriate, and reference the quoted shell variable from run.
limitations: Only direct run commands in checked-in .github/workflows YAML files are inspected; sibling env mappings and non-run block-scalar contents are not shell commands.

String and choice inputs, github.event fields, and github.head_ref are treated as untrusted. Complete boolean and number input expressions declared under on.workflow_dispatch or on.workflow_call are excluded; github.event.inputs aliases require workflow_dispatch declarations. Choice declarations do not prove shell-safe values or API-side option validation. Complete event.number, event.before, event.after, pull-request number and head/base SHA, workflow-run head SHA, and the trusted base repository default-branch expressions are excluded. Names, refs, titles, property extensions, and expressions mixing safe and untrusted values remain reportable.
The rule does not perform cross-step data-flow analysis or fully parse GitHub expression syntax.
